# @ic-reactor/candid

> Reactors for canisters whose Candid interface is only known at run time:
> fetch and parse a canister's Candid, call its methods dynamically, and build
> form and result metadata from it. For explorers, dev tools and generic UIs.

Applies to `@ic-reactor/candid` 3.12.5.

Read this file from `node_modules/@ic-reactor/candid/llms.txt` when writing
code against the installed version. The complete guide for every package is
https://ic-reactor.b3pay.net/llms-full.txt, and behaviour changes are in
https://github.com/B3Pay/ic-reactor/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @ic-reactor/candid @ic-reactor/core @icp-sdk/core @tanstack/query-core
```

`ClientManager` comes from `@ic-reactor/core` and needs a `QueryClient` from
`@tanstack/query-core`. The first is only a transitive dependency of this
package, which pnpm does not let the app import, and the second an optional
peer of core, so list both. A React app imports
`ClientManager` from `@ic-reactor/react` and `QueryClient` from
`@tanstack/react-query` instead. `@ic-reactor/parser` comes with this package
and loads on the first parse, as a chunk of its own.

## Setup and Usage

```ts
import { CandidReactor, MetadataReactor } from "@ic-reactor/candid"
import { ClientManager } from "@ic-reactor/core"
import { QueryClient } from "@tanstack/query-core"

const clientManager = new ClientManager({
  queryClient: new QueryClient(),
  agentOptions: { host: "https://ic0.app" },
})

// Any canister: fetch its Candid, then call it like a typed Reactor
export async function symbolOf(canisterId: string) {
  const token = new CandidReactor({ clientManager, canisterId, name: "token" })
  await token.initialize() // fetches and parses the canister's Candid
  console.log(token.getMethodNames())
  return token.fetchQuery({ functionName: "icrc1_symbol" }) // cached
}

// One method from its signature, without fetching the whole interface
export function nameOf(canisterId: string) {
  const token = new CandidReactor({ clientManager, canisterId, name: "token" })
  return token.queryDynamic({
    functionName: "icrc1_name",
    candid: "() -> (text) query",
  })
}

// Form metadata: fields, defaults and a zod schema for the arguments
export async function transferForm(canisterId: string) {
  const ledger = new MetadataReactor({
    clientManager,
    canisterId,
    name: "ledger",
  })
  await ledger.initialize()
  return ledger.getInputMeta("icrc1_transfer")
}
```

## When to Use What

| Need                                          | Use                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Fetch or parse a canister's Candid            | `CandidAdapter` (`getCandidDefinition`, `fetchCandidSource`)                  |
| Call a canister known only at run time        | `CandidReactor` (raw values), `CandidDisplayReactor` (display values)         |
| Call one method from its Candid signature     | `registerMethod`, or `queryDynamic` / `callDynamic` / `fetchQueryDynamic`     |
| Build a form for a method's arguments         | `MetadataReactor` / `MetadataDisplayReactor`, `getInputMeta(method)`          |
| Render a result generically                   | `getOutputMeta(method)`                                                       |
| Low-level metadata from an `IDL.ServiceClass` | `CandidFormVisitor`                                                           |
| Another canister with the same interface      | `reactor.forCanister(canisterId)`                                             |
| The interface is known at build time          | generated declarations with `@ic-reactor/react` or `@ic-reactor/core` instead |

## Details

- `CandidReactor` extends the core `Reactor`: after `initialize()` or
  `registerMethod()`, `callMethod`, `fetchQuery`, `getQueryOptions` and
  `invalidateQueries` work as usual, and the React hooks accept it.
- Pass `candid: "service : { ... }"` to the constructor to skip the network
  fetch, or `idlFactory` when you already have one.
- Without a service type parameter, a `CandidDisplayReactor`'s display-side
  args, validator args and results are `unknown`: cast them to the display
  shape, or pass `new CandidDisplayReactor<Service>(...)` when the interface is
  known at build time.
- `reactor.forCanister(canisterId)` works on all four reactors. The sibling
  starts with this reactor's interface, Candid source and adapter (and its
  validators or metadata), so a sibling of an initialized reactor is ready to
  call. A method registered later stays on the reactor it was registered on.
- Parsing uses the local WASM parser; when it cannot load, the adapter falls
  back to compiling through the didjs canister, which keeps upstream behaviour
  for a field named like a numeric id (`_0_`).
- The form visitors accept `""` for a `text` field; principals, numbers,
  formatted text fields and a func reference's method name must be filled in.
- On `MetadataReactor`, a func record's `defaultArgs` are Candid values ready
  for `callMethod` on a reactor built from the node's `funcClass`;
  `MetadataDisplayReactor` gives display values.
- `isPrincipalId` accepts canonical principal text of at most 29 bytes.
- An adapter keeps no subscription on the `ClientManager`, so dropped reactors
  need no cleanup; `adapter.unsubscribe` is a deprecated no-op.

## Do Not

- Use this package for a canister whose `.did` you have at build time;
  generate declarations and use typed reactors.
- Call a dynamic reactor's methods before `initialize()` or
  `registerMethod()` has run for them.
- Hand-build a reactor per canister of one interface; use `forCanister`.
- Deep-import `@ic-reactor/parser/dist/...`; the adapter loads the parser.
- Call `adapter.unsubscribe()`; it does nothing.
